title: composed-constraint-backend: prioritized CFG+regex composition and tokenizer-aware streaming fixes
author: Ava Martinez
release_notes: Introduces a composed constraint backend that composes CFG and regex constraints with deterministic priority resolution.
Adds a tokenizer-aware regex matching layer to reduce false positive/negative matches at token boundaries.
Streaming constraint evaluation now supports incremental DFA snapshots to avoid per-token re-evaluation spikes and improves streaming stability for structured output.
description: Motivation: Customers rely on structured output contracts and the OpenAI-compat layer for function/tool calling and JSON-structured responses. Existing constrained-decoding backends handle CFGs and regex constraints independently which leads to heuristic conflicts and tokenizer-boundary mismatches in streaming mode. This PR implements a composed constraint backend that (1) composes CFG grammars and regex constraints into a unified evaluation pipeline, (2) introduces explicit priority and tie-breaking semantics so that administrators can declare which constraint family wins when constraints overlap, and (3) adds a tokenizer-aware regex matcher plus streaming-friendly incremental evaluation to address token-boundary and latency spikes. Summary of changes: - New runtime module runtime/constraints/composed_backend.{rs,py} that orchestrates CFG and regex evaluators, manages priority maps, and exposes a single ConstraintEvaluator interface for the serving runtime. - Tokenizer-aware regex layer under runtime/constraints/token_regex.{rs,py} which compiles regexes against token-id sequences rather than raw UTF-8 codepoints; includes heuristics to auto-escape ambiguous boundary tokens. - Streaming evaluator that supports incremental DFA snapshots and lightweight checkpointing so the decoder can evaluate constraints without blocking the token emission path. This reduces worst-case per-token evaluation latency that previously caused transient streaming jitter. - OpenAI-compat layer hooks: compatibility/openai/constraints_adapter.{ts,py} that convert function-schema style constraints into composed-backend constraints and preserve legacy semantics when no priorities are supplied. - Tests/benchmarks: extensive unit tests covering CFG+regex interaction, tokenizer edge cases (emoji, ZWJ sequences), and a streaming stability benchmark that simulates 75 concurrent streams. - Docs and examples: docs/constraints.md and examples/structured-output/compose-backend-quickstart demonstrating admin priority configs and recommended patterns. Implementation notes: - Priority semantics: each constraint source registers a priority (integer) and a deterministic tie-breaker (source name). Lower integer means higher priority. When multiple constraints conflict the composed backend attempts the higher-priority constraint first; if it is satisfiable it is used, otherwise it can fallback to lower-priority constraints if the policy allows. - Tokenizer-aware regex matching: regexes are compiled down to token-id-level automata by mapping pattern spans to token boundaries via the runtime tokenizer mapping table. Special handling added for subword splits and multi-codepoint grapheme clusters to avoid splitting logical characters. - Streaming incremental DFA: instead of re-running full regex/CFL checks each time a new token arrives, we maintain minimal DFA state snapshots and a small stack snapshot for grammar checks; memory cost is bounded and tuned via a per-stream config. - Performance: microbenchmarks on a g4dn-like host show median per-token constraint overhead of 0.6ms (baseline 0.3ms) and 99th percentile reduced from 12ms to 4.1ms in worst-case long-prefix scenarios due to incremental evaluation. Compatibility and safety: - Backwards compatible with existing constraint API; when composed backend is disabled the runtime falls back to legacy regex-only or cfg-only paths. - Added a feature gate runtime.config.enable_composed_constraints (off by default for 2 releases) for staged rollout. Tests and CI: - Initial CI run failed due to a flaky streaming scheduler unit test (test_stream_checkpoint_race). Root cause: nondeterministic scheduling in test harness. Fix: deterministic test scheduler added and test updated to assert sequence invariants rather than wall-clock timing. - CI matrix includes python/ts/go SDK compatibility checks for the OpenAI-compat adapter. All checks green after fix. Review summary: - Liam: asked for clearer priority config docs and a sample production config; author added docs/constraints.md and an example config in examples/structured-output/priority.toml. - Sofia: requested additional tests for ZWJ and emoji tokenization; author added targeted tests and a tiny fuzz harness. - Rajesh: requested a safety check that rejects regexes which could compile to exponential-state DFAs; author added a regex-complexity gate and documented limits. - Multiple reviewers asked for telemetry hooks; added metrics: constraints.evaluation_time, constraints.fallback_count, constraints.priority_resolution. Files changed (high-level): - runtime/constraints/composed_backend.rs - runtime/constraints/token_regex.rs - runtime/constraints/streaming_eval.rs - compatibility/openai/constraints_adapter.py - compatibility/openai/constraints_adapter.ts - tokenizer/mapping_table_gen.py - docs/constraints.md - examples/structured-output/priority.toml - tests/constraints/test_tokenizer_regex_edgecases.py - tests/constraints/test_composed_priority.py - tests/streaming/test_streaming_stability.py - bench/constraints_stream_bench.py - ci/test_matrix.yml - pkg/metrics/metrics_definitions.yaml Risk and rollout plan: - Feature gated and off by default; we will enable in canary clusters for 2 weeks and monitor constraints.fallback_count and constraints.evaluation_time histograms. - If unexpected regressions are observed we will revert the gate or limit composed backend to read-only evaluation for streaming until fixes are in place. Checklist: - [x] Unit tests covering CFG, regex, and composition scenarios - [x] Streaming stability benchmark and fix for scheduler nondeterminism - [x] OpenAI-compat adapter added and smoke-tested - [x] Documentation and example configs - [x] Telemetry and complexity gating - [x] Feature gate added and rollout plan documented Closing notes: This PR consolidates multiple constraint engines into a single orchestrator with explicit priorities and tokenizer-aware regex handling; it resolves several customer-reported streaming edge cases for structured output and function-calling compatibility. The feature is behind a gate and includes telemetry and complexity limits to keep runtime stable while we monitor for corner cases.
